Maple Glazed Pork Tenderloin with Roasted Vegetables

By Kaleb WysePublished Sep 27, 2026
No ratings yet

Fall dinner, all on one pan! Maple glazed pork tenderloin roasts with sweet potatoes, Brussels sprouts, and crispy pancetta.

Prep Time 20 minutes mins
Cook Time 50 minutes mins
Total Time 3 hours hrs 20 minutes mins

Why I Love This Pork Tenderloin

When I start bringing fall flavors into the kitchen, this is exactly the meal I want to make. Sweet potatoes and Brussels sprouts roast alongside pork tenderloin, with some spices in the vegetables and maple syrup in the marinade. Could that sound any more like the perfect fall meal?! Yes, there’s some sweetness, but the combination of Dijon mustard, apple cider vinegar, and soy sauce keeps everything savory, just like dinner should be.

For easy dinners, I love using ingredients that do more than one job. The pancetta gives us flavorful fat for searing the pork, then becomes a final crispy topping. Plus, a maple-Dijon marinade flavors the pork and becomes a glossy finishing sauce, while the vegetables roast alongside the meat.

Get the pork marinating earlier in the day, and you have a dinner that works just as well for a weeknight as it does for company.

Here’s why you’ll love this fall recipe:

  • A complete dinner – The pork, sweet potatoes, and Brussels sprouts make a main dish and vegetables in one.
  • Sweet and savory flavor – Maple syrup balances mustard, vinegar, garlic, and soy sauce.
  • Easy to put together – Start marinating earlier in the day, prepare the vegetables beforehand, and dinner comes together quickly.

Maple Glazed Pork Tenderloin Ingredients

The ingredients in this recipe are all about amplifying the feeling of fall, while providing a delicious and filling dinner:

  • Apple cider vinegar – Adds tang to balance the maple syrup and richness of the sauce.
  • Maple syrup – Use pure maple syrup for its flavor, rather than pancake syrup.
  • Olive oil – Goes into the marinade and helps the vegetables roast.
  • Soy sauce – Adds salt and savory depth to the pork and finishing sauce.
  • Garlic – Grating helps the garlic distribute throughout the marinade.
  • Dijon mustard – Adds tang and a little sharpness that works so well with maple.
  • Pork tenderloin – Choose tenderloins of similar size so they cook at about the same rate. Pork loin is a different, larger cut and needs different timing.
  • Sweet potatoes, Brussels sprouts, and red onion – A trio of vegetables that work well together and feel like the fall season.
  • Kosher salt and black pepper – Season the vegetables and the marinade.
  • Ground allspice, ground mustard seed, garlic powder, and onion powder – A delicious combination that forms a warm spice blend. You can crush whole mustard seeds with a mortar and pestle if you don’t have ground.
  • Pancetta – Provides fat for searing the tenderloin and crisp pieces for the topping.
  • Unsalted butter – Whisked into the reduced sauce off the heat for a perfect finish.

The full amount of each ingredient can be found in the recipe card below.

How to Make Maple Glazed Pork Tenderloin

There are 6 steps to make this pork tenderloin recipe:

Step 1: Marinate the pork – Combine the vinegar, maple syrup, olive oil, soy sauce, garlic, and Dijon mustard in a large resealable bag. Add the tenderloins, seal, and gently massage to coat. Set the bag in a dish and refrigerate for 2-8 hours.

Step 2: Prepare the vegetables – Toss the Brussels sprouts, sweet potatoes, and red onion with olive oil. Add the salt, black pepper, allspice, ground mustard seed, garlic powder, and onion powder. Stir to coat evenly, then set aside.

Step 3: Cook the pancetta and sear the pork – Heat a large stovetop-safe roasting pan over medium heat. Cook the pancetta until browned and crisp, 4-6 minutes. Remove with a spoon, keeping the rendered fat in the pan. Remove the pork from the marinade, letting the excess drip off, and reserve the marinade for the sauce. Sear the tenderloins in the pancetta fat until browned, about 3-5 minutes per side. Transfer the pork to a plate and set aside.

Step 4: Roast the vegetables – Add the seasoned vegetables to the roasting pan and spread into as even a layer as possible. Roast in a preheated 425°F oven for 12-15 minutes, until beginning to soften and brown.

Step 5: Finish roasting and rest – Place the tenderloins over the partially roasted vegetables and return the pan to the oven. Begin checking the pork after about 15 minutes, and roast until each tenderloin reaches 145°F in its thickest part and the sweet potatoes are tender. Remove the pork and let it rest for 10 minutes before slicing.

Step 6: Make the glaze and serve – While the pork is roasting, pour the reserved marinade into a saucepan. Bring to a full boil and boil for a few minutes before reducing to a simmer. Continue cooking until reduced by about half and slightly thickened. Remove from the heat and whisk in the cold butter a little at a time. Remove any kitchen twine, slice the rested pork, and spoon on the glaze. Finish with the reserved pancetta and serve with the roasted vegetables.

Recipe Tips

  • Form the tenderloins – If a tenderloin has a very thin tail, fold it underneath and secure with kitchen twine before marinating. This will help the meat cook properly when roasting.
  • Use a pan that can handle both cooking stages – Check that your roasting pan is rated for direct stovetop heat. If it isn’t, sear in a skillet and transfer the rendered fat and vegetables to a large roasting pan for the oven.
  • Let excess marinade drip off – Too much liquid in the pan makes it harder to brown the pork. Keep an eye on the maple syrup as it caramelizes so the browned bits don’t turn black.
  • Check both tenderloins – One can finish before the other, even when they look similar. Remove each when it reaches the correct temperature when checked with an instant-read thermometer.
  • Look for a pourable glaze – The sauce should lightly coat the meat. It doesn’t need to thicken like candy, and the flavor concentrates as it reduces. If it becomes too thick or intense, whisk in a little water.

Frequently Asked Questions

Can I use pork loin instead of pork tenderloins?

This recipe is written for two 1-pound pork tenderloins. A pork loin is larger and will take longer to cook, so it won’t follow the same times listed in the recipe. I’d recommend using tenderloins to keep the pork and vegetable timing the same.

Why do the vegetables roast before the pork goes back in?

The sweet potatoes need more time to become tender than the seared tenderloins need to finish cooking. Giving the vegetables a head start helps ensure you get the vegetables roasted properly without overcooking the tenderloins.

Can I really use the marinade as a sauce?

Yes, but you must boil it first because it touched raw pork. Bring it to a full boil for a few minutes before simmering it down into the finishing glaze. Never spoon the uncooked used marinade over the finished meal.

What temperature should pork tenderloin reach?

Cook it to 140°F in the thickest part before removing it from the heat, then let it rest for 10 minutes before slicing, which will bring the internal temperature up to 145°F. Check each tenderloin separately with a thermometer to ensure it reaches the finished temperature.

Follow These Tips

Serving & Storage

Serving – Spoon the vegetables onto a platter and arrange the sliced pork over the top. Drizzle with some of the maple glaze, scatter over the cooked pancetta, and put any remaining glaze in a container to serve at the table.

The sweet potatoes and Brussels sprouts make this a meal, but you could add a fall-inspired salad or some French bread as an accompaniment.

Refrigerate – Refrigerate leftovers within 2 hours in an airtight container. Store the pork, vegetables, and sauce for up to 3-4 days. Keeping the sauce separate makes it easier to portion and reheat.

Reheat – Reheat any leftovers in the oven at 325°F or in the microwave.

Maple Glazed Pork Tenderloin with Roasted Vegetables

By Kaleb
No ratings yet
Fall dinner, all on one pan! Maple glazed pork tenderloin roasts with sweet potatoes, Brussels sprouts, and crispy pancetta.
Prep: 20 minutes mins
Cook: 50 minutes mins
Marinate: 2 hours hrs
Total: 3 hours hrs 20 minutes mins
Servings: 8 servings
SaveSaved Pin Print
Save this recipe!
Get this sent to your inbox, plus get new recipes from us every week!

Ingredients

  • ¼ cup apple cider vinegar
  • ¼ cup maple syrup
  • ½ cup + 2 tablespoons olive oil separated
  • ⅓ cup soy sauce
  • 3 cloves garlic grated
  • 2 tablespoons Dijon mustard
  • 2 1-pound pork tenderloins
  • 2 medium sweet potatoes (about 1 pound) scrubbed clean, not peeled, cut into ½-inch pieces
  • 3 cups cleaned and halved Brussels sprouts (about 1 pound)
  • 1 medium red onion roughly chopped
  • 1 ½ teaspoons kosher salt
  • ¾ teaspoon freshly ground black pepper
  • ½ teaspoon ground allspice
  • ½ teaspoon ground mustard seed
  • ½ teaspoon garlic powder
  • ½ teaspoon onion powder
  • 4 ounces diced pancetta
  • 2 tablespoons cold unsalted butter
Prevent your screen from going dark

Instructions 

  • Make the marinade: In a large resealable plastic bag, combine the vinegar, maple syrup, ½ cup olive oil, soy sauce, garlic, and mustard. Add the tenderloins and seal the bag. Gently massage the tenderloins to ensure they are evenly coated with the marinade. Place the bag on a dish and refrigerate for 2-8 hours.
    ¼ cup apple cider vinegar, ¼ cup maple syrup, ½ cup + 2 tablespoons olive oil, ⅓ cup soy sauce, 3 cloves garlic, 2 tablespoons Dijon mustard, 2 1-pound pork tenderloins
  • Preheat the oven to 425°F.
  • Prepare the vegetables. In a large bowl, combine the sweet potatoes, Brussels sprouts, and red onion. Toss with 2 tablespoons olive oil and add the salt, black pepper, allspice, ground mustard seed, garlic powder, and onion powder. Set aside.
    2 medium sweet potatoes (about 1 pound), 3 cups cleaned and halved Brussels sprouts (about 1 pound), 1 ½ teaspoons kosher salt, ¾ teaspoon freshly ground black pepper, ½ teaspoon ground allspice, ½ teaspoon ground mustard seed, ½ teaspoon garlic powder, ½ teaspoon onion powder, 1 medium red onion
  • Sear the tenderloins: Heat a roasting pan over medium heat and add the pancetta. Stir and cook until the pancetta is browned and crisp, 4-6 minutes. Remove the pancetta with a slotted spoon, leaving the rendered fat in the roasting pan, and set aside. Remove the tenderloins from the marinade, reserving the marinade. Add the tenderloin to the roasting pan and sear until well browned, 3-5 minutes. Turn over and sear the other side until browned, 3-5 minutes. Turn off the heat, remove the tenderloins, and set them aside.
    4 ounces diced pancetta
  • Cook: Add the prepared vegetables to the roasting pan and place in the preheated 425°F oven. Roast until the vegetables are slightly tender and beginning to brown, 12-15 minutes. Add the tenderloins to the partially roasted vegetables and return to the oven. Roast until the pork registers 140°F and the sweet potatoes are tender, 15-20 minutes. Remove from the oven and let the tenderloins rest for 10 minutes. During this time, carryover cooking will bring the pork to a final temperature of 145°F.
  • Make the sauce: While the tenderloins are roasting, add the reserved marinade to a saucepan. Bring the marinade to a boil and reduce to a simmer. Cook until it is slightly thickened and reduced by half, 6-8 minutes. Remove from the heat and whisk in the butter. Pour over the meat, sprinkle on the reserved pancetta, and serve.
    2 tablespoons cold unsalted butter
